ask: build a production llm classifier that routes inbound support tickets to 8 different engineering teams based on ticket content. requirements: confidence score for each prediction, a fallback to a human queue when confidence is below 0.7, structured json output that a downstream service can parse without error handling for refusals, injection defense since users can write anything in ticket body, and a test harness with at least 50 labeled examples per category. describe the full system design before writing any code
rationale: Production classifier at scale; system prompt for rules; structured output; injection defense; eval harness built in.

ask: design a real-time content moderation system for a social platform with 100k posts per day. the system needs to classify each post as safe, nsfw, graphic_violence, hate_speech, or spam within 500ms. it should handle posts in english, spanish, and portuguese. the output must be structured json that downstream services parse programmatically. any refusal or timeout from the llm must be handled gracefully without crashing the pipeline. also flag posts where user text appears to be attempting to manipulate the classifier itself
rationale: Multi-class moderation at scale; injection defense for classifier manipulation attempts; structured output; refusal handling.

ask: analyze 18 months of user behavior data across 6 product features — daily active usage, session length, feature adoption rate, and 30-day retention cohorts by acquisition channel. the data is in bigquery. i need to know: which features correlate most strongly with 90-day retention, which features users try once and abandon within 3 sessions, whether there are cohort differences by acquisition channel, and any surprising patterns that might change our product roadmap. structure your analysis plan before running queries
rationale: Complex cohort analysis across features; decompose by feature then synthesize cross-feature patterns.

ask: i'm pasting a 300-page technical requirements document for a new payments platform rebuild. produce a structured analysis with: an implementation roadmap with quarterly milestones, a risk register scored by likelihood and impact, effort estimates by component in engineer-weeks, and a list of requirements that are contradictory ambiguous or technically infeasible as written. output each section separately in a format that can be shared directly with our engineering managers
rationale: Long doc first (T22 instruction placement); outline-first for structure; ambiguous specs are guaranteed; structured per-section output.

ask: research the feasibility of replacing our nightly batch analytics pipeline with a real-time streaming approach using apache kafka and apache flink. we currently process about 2tb of event data per night across 40 different event types, have a 4-person data team with no kafka experience, and our product team wants dashboard results available within 5 minutes of events occurring instead of the next morning. give me a structured feasibility assessment covering technical fit, team capability gaps, migration risk, and an honest estimate of how long this would take
rationale: Streaming migration feasibility study; plan-and-execute for structured analysis; Kafka/Flink ecosystem evolves.

ask: evaluate github copilot cursor sourcegraph cody continue.dev and tabnine for an enterprise engineering team of 120 developers. evaluation criteria: ide support across vscode and jetbrains, context window size for large codebases, on-premises deployment option, soc2 type 2 compliance, cost per seat at volume, and quality specifically on our python and typescript stack. produce a decision matrix with scores and a final recommendation with justification. we need to make a decision before the end of this quarter
rationale: Tool evaluation matrix; contrastive format with scoring; fast-moving space with pricing changes; structured output for stakeholders.

ask: i want to build something combining mcp__filesystem__read_file mcp__github__create_pull_request mcp__slack__post_message and the anthropic agents sdk. the goal is an automated code review bot that reads changed files from a pr, runs analysis, posts inline comments via github, and sends a summary to slack. what is the best architecture for this, what are the failure modes i should handle, and how would i test this system before running it on real pull requests from my team
rationale: HARD: names many MCP tools; agent SDK is recent; plan-and-execute for architecture; ambiguous scope without review criteria.

ask: design a multi-tenant ai agent platform from scratch. each tenant needs isolated tool permissions so tenant a cannot call tenant b's tools, per-tenant rate limiting tied to their subscription tier, shared memory across agent sessions within a tenant but strict isolation between tenants, full audit logging of every tool call and agent decision for compliance, and the ability for each tenant to plug in their own custom tools via a registration api. we plan to serve 100 enterprise clients, some with hipaa and soc2 requirements. what is the architecture and what are the hardest engineering problems to solve first
rationale: Complex multi-component platform; plan artifact essential; extended thinking for compliance tradeoffs; ambiguous without agent SDK choice.

ask: design a complete technical specification for integrating stripe payments into our saas product. cover: api key management and rotation strategy, webhook signature verification and replay attack prevention, idempotency key design for retry safety, the full state machine for subscription lifecycle events, failed payment retry logic with configurable schedules, refund and dispute handling flows, pci compliance scope reduction approach, and a rollback plan if we need to remove stripe. include ascii sequence diagrams for the happy path and the main failure paths
rationale: Payment design doc; outline-first; definition of done for each component; webhook injection defense; rollback is destructive.

ask: i have a google l5 software engineer interview in 3 weeks and i'm weak on graphs dynamic programming and system design. i'm strong in python and have 5 years backend experience. i have 2 hours free each weekday. build me a detailed study plan broken down by week and day, covering data structures and algorithms with specific problem types to practice, one system design topic per week with a mock design exercise, and behavioral prep for the google format. tell me which resources to use and how to track my progress
rationale: Multi-topic prep plan with calendar decomposition; plan artifact before practice; iterative feedback loop by design.

ask: design a gdpr-compliant user data deletion system that cascades across our postgres database, s3 object storage with user uploads, elasticsearch search indices, and segment analytics warehouse. deletion requests must complete within 30 days per regulation, every deletion must be logged in an immutable audit trail, partial failures in one system must not silently skip the others, we need to handle the edge case where someone deletes their account and then creates a new one with the same email, and the system must produce a compliance report on demand. we have 1.2 million registered users
rationale: Cross-system deletion cascade; irreversible; definition of done critical; GDPR requirements and enforcement guidance evolve.

ask: help me figure out why our recommendation engine is showing the same 10 items to almost every user. this started 3 days ago after a data pipeline change. i'm attaching the recommendation model code, the feature generation pipeline that feeds it, the serving layer that calls it, sample user feature vectors before and after the pipeline change, and the output distribution showing the collapse. help me form hypotheses in order of likelihood and tell me exactly what to check to validate each one
rationale: ML debugging across pipeline stages; systematic hypothesis decomposition by component; ambiguous cause without full data.

ask: we just discovered that our s3 bucket containing customer pii including emails and hashed passwords was misconfigured as publicly readable for approximately 6 hours last night. i'm the engineering lead and it's 2am. walk me through exactly what to do in the next 30 minutes, the next 4 hours, and the next 24 hours. include: who to wake up immediately, what evidence to preserve before touching anything, what we need to tell legal and the board, the notification obligations we likely have under gdpr and ccpa, and how to prevent this class of misconfiguration permanently
rationale: Security incident response; time-ordered plan essential; GDPR/CCPA notification requirements need current regulatory guidance.

ask: conduct a thorough build vs buy analysis for our core ml platform. we need: model training orchestration with experiment tracking, a model registry with versioning, and a serving layer that handles 500 predictions per second. our team has 4 ml engineers who are strong in pytorch and python but have never built infrastructure. our annual ml infra budget is $400k. our 3-year roadmap has us going from 10 models to 200 models. i need a recommendation with cost projections for both paths and an honest assessment of the risks of each
rationale: Build-vs-buy with budget, team, and roadmap constraints; plan-and-execute for cost-benefit; MLOps market evolves.

ask: we need to migrate our 40k line python 2.7 codebase to python 3.12. there are no unit tests, several third-party dependencies that were python 2 only and may not have python 3 equivalents, and we cannot take the service down for more than 4 hours total during the migration. the service handles about 3000 requests per hour. propose the safest possible migration approach, break it into phases, tell me what the biggest risks are in each phase, and describe how you would validate correctness without a test suite
rationale: Large migration without tests is high-risk; plan-and-execute mandatory; ambiguous compatibility without dependency audit.

ask: brainstorm a comprehensive product strategy for an ai-powered developer productivity tool that we want to take from zero to 10k paying users in 18 months. think through: what specific pain points to solve first and why, what the ideal initial user persona looks like and where to find them, what the minimum viable version looks like versus what you build in month 12, how to price it for a dev tools market where free tiers are expected, and what metrics actually predict whether developers will pay for productivity tools. push past the obvious ideas
rationale: Deep product strategy ideation; tree-of-thoughts for divergent directions; self-critique culls surface-level ideas.

ask: ideate on novel architectures for a multi-agent system where agents specialize in different parts of a software development workflow: planning, coding, testing, and code review. go beyond the obvious serial pipeline and think about how agents could work in parallel, how they should hand off context to each other, what shared memory or state looks like, how to handle disagreements between agents, and what the failure modes are when one agent produces bad output. generate at least 3 fundamentally different architectures and evaluate the tradeoffs
rationale: Novel architecture ideation; tree-of-thoughts for multiple design directions; extended thinking for deep tradeoff analysis.

ask: i need to pitch our engineering team on adopting a monorepo structure and i expect significant pushback. brainstorm the strongest possible counterarguments our senior engineers will make — not strawmen, the real objections from people who have been burned by monorepos before. then for each objection generate two responses: one that directly rebuts it with evidence, and one that acknowledges it and shows how we would mitigate it. this will help me prepare for a contentious all-hands discussion
rationale: Argument preparation; red-team generates strongest counterarguments; self-critique ensures responses are substantive not dismissive.

ask: write the complete prompt engineering package for a contract clause extraction agent that will process ndas and service agreements for a legal team. deliver: a system prompt, five few-shot examples that cover hard edge cases including implied clauses, cross-references to other sections, and missing clauses that need to be flagged as absent, a json output schema with every field documented including its null behavior, twenty test cases including ten hard negatives where the clause is absent or ambiguous, and a scoring rubric for evaluating output quality. the agent will run on documents from unknown sources so injection defense matters
rationale: Full prompt package; few-shot with hard edge cases; schema for legal downstream; injection defense for arbitrary contract content.

ask: build a multi-agent content pipeline using the anthropic agents sdk with four specialized agents: agent one researches a given topic using web search tools, agent two drafts an article based on the research, agent three rewrites the draft for seo using keyword density and heading structure analysis, and agent four formats the final output for the wordpress rest api. each agent hands off a structured context object to the next. describe the system design, the handoff schema between agents, how you handle a failure in any stage, and how you would test the full pipeline end to end
rationale: Multi-agent pipeline; decomposition into agent stages; output chaining; injection defense for web-sourced research content.

ask: design an llm-powered routing system that reads incoming user messages and predicts: the task tier, the appropriate response pool, the task type from a vocabulary of 16 types, zero to two prompting techniques that would improve the prompt, and a set of boolean trigger flags. the system needs to output structured json, handle edge cases like ambiguous inputs and non-english messages gracefully, and produce confidence scores so a fallback can be triggered when the router is uncertain. write the system prompt, output schema, and 10 test cases including hard ones
rationale: Router system prompt design; structured output essential; system prompt placement for stability; ambiguous inputs are a core hard case.

ask: write a 1500-word technical blog post for our engineering newsletter about the transition from synchronous to async database operations in fastapi. audience is our 12 internal backend engineers with varying async experience. cover: why we made the change, the specific friction we hit with sqlalchemy sync drivers in an async context, how we solved it using asyncpg and connection pooling, what we learned about testing async code with pytest-asyncio, and give three concrete before-and-after code examples. tone should be collegial and honest about what was painful
rationale: Long technical blog; outline-first for section structure; internal audience spec shapes honesty and vocabulary.

ask: i need to present to our board of directors next week making the case for a $2m investment in ai infrastructure this year. help me build the 12-slide narrative. the audience is five board members: two technical and three non-technical. i need: competitive positioning against peers who are already moving, a credible roi estimate with assumptions made explicit, a risk section that addresses the board's concern about building on rapidly changing foundation models, and a build vs buy recommendation for the three core infrastructure components. include specific market data points and benchmarks
rationale: Board presentation; outline-first for slide structure; mixed-audience spec; current market benchmarks needed; critique loop for credibility.

ask: write a 2000-word technical blog post about how the model context protocol is changing the llm tooling ecosystem. the audience is senior engineers who use claude daily but haven't studied mcp internals. include: what problem mcp solves that wasn't solved before, how the protocol works mechanically including the server-client model and tool registration, a concrete working example showing a filesystem server being used by an agent, an honest assessment of current limitations and rough edges, and a prediction about what the ecosystem looks like in 18 months. avoid hype
rationale: Long technical piece; outline-first; precise senior-engineer audience spec; MCP is very current; critique loop catches hype.

ask: write a comprehensive technical design document for our new microservices event bus. the document will be reviewed by senior engineers and architects before implementation starts. it needs to cover: problem statement and why we're moving away from direct api calls, technology selection rationale comparing kafka rabbitmq and redis streams, the proposed event schema and versioning strategy, consumer group design and failure handling, observability approach for event tracing across services, and a phased migration plan from our current synchronous system. use headers and tables where appropriate
rationale: Technical design doc for engineering review; outline-first for structure; definition of done (review sign-off) shapes completeness.

ask: draft a security incident report for our customers explaining that we had a data exposure event last month. the exposure lasted 6 hours, involved access logs but not payment data or passwords, and affected 340 customers who have already been notified individually. the report should be honest about what happened, clearly explain the technical root cause without being condescending, describe what we've done to prevent recurrence, and close with what affected customers should do. we need this to be factual and calm, not defensive or over-apologetic
rationale: Customer-facing incident communication; audience spec (affected customers); outline-first; critique loop for tone calibration.

ask: write a 20-page technical due diligence report on our engineering organization's readiness for a series b investment. the investors will share this with their technical advisors who will scrutinize it. cover: codebase quality indicators and technical debt assessment, scalability bottlenecks we're aware of and our plans, security posture and any known vulnerabilities we're addressing, team capability and key person risk, infrastructure costs and trajectory, and a candid section on what we would do differently if starting over. be honest — investors already know we're not perfect
rationale: High-stakes investor document; outline-first for completeness; expert audience spec (technical advisors); critique loop for credibility.

ask: help!! prod database is down i need to restore from the rds snapshot taken at 3am this morning — what is the exact sequence of aws cli commands i need to run right now, what should i check before i start to avoid making things worse, and what's the fastest path to getting the service back without corrupting any data that was written between 3am and when the db went down
rationale: HARD: urgent casual language masks a destructive restore operation; ambiguous which snapshot instance and recovery point objective.

ask: write a comprehensive system prompt for a coding assistant that should: stay strictly in scope and refuse non-coding questions gracefully, use a collaborative tone that feels like pair programming not lecturing, always explain the reasoning behind code suggestions not just the code, ask one clarifying question when requirements are ambiguous rather than guessing, adapt its explanation depth based on whether the user seems to be a beginner or expert, and handle the case where a user pastes untrusted code or files that might contain injection attempts. also write 5 test cases that would verify each of these behaviors
rationale: Comprehensive agent system prompt; constraints define scope and persona; system placement; injection defense for pasted code.
